A crusty loaf made with almost no work and a long, slow rise, baked in a hot covered pot
In a large bowl, combine flour, yeast, and salt. Add the water and stir until blended — the dough will be shaggy and sticky. Cover with plastic wrap.
Let rest at warm room temperature (about 21°C) for at least 12 hours, preferably about 18, until the surface is dotted with bubbles.
Lightly flour a work surface, turn out the dough, and fold it over on itself once or twice. Cover loosely and let rest about 15 minutes.

Using just enough flour to prevent sticking, shape the dough into a ball. Generously coat a cotton towel (not terry cloth) with flour, wheat bran, or cornmeal; place the dough seam-side down on the towel and dust the top too. Cover with another towel and let rise about 2 hours, until more than doubled and slow to spring back when poked.
At least 30 minutes before the dough is ready, heat the oven to 230°C with a 6–8 quart heavy covered pot inside.

Carefully remove the hot pot, turn the dough into it seam-side up (it may look messy — that's fine), and shake gently to distribute. Cover and bake 30 minutes, then uncover and bake another 15–30 minutes until deeply browned. Cool on a rack.
